articles.title: Predictors of Limited Weight-Bearing Dorsiflexion Following Total Ankle Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Thomas GM, McCahon JAS, Dulitzki Y, Chen Z, Parekh SG, Daniel JN, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective primary total ankle replacement
articles.sample_size: 175 patients (111 with limited dorsiflexion, 64 with full dorsiflexion)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative dorsiflexion range of motion, functional ability scores and pain scores
articles.take_home: How much your ankle could bend upwards before surgery was the only reliable predictor of how much it would bend after ankle replacement surgery. Surgeons should discuss expected movement with patients beforehand to manage expectations.

articles.title: The Amount of Peroneus Longus Insertion Resection With Modified Lapidus Procedure for Severe Hallux Valgus: Comparative Radiographic Study of 2 Different Osteotomy Methods.
articles.authors: Sakurai S, Nakasa T, Ikuta Y, Ishibashi S, Moriwaki D, Chujo T, et al.
articles.outcomes: Amount of peroneus longus insertion resected during modified Lapidus procedure using two different osteotomy methods; intermetatarsal angle correction; first ray stability
articles.take_home: Cutting the bone at the first metatarsal (M-method) removes more than half of the peroneus longus muscle attachment, whilst cutting at the cuneiform bone (C-method) preserves more of this important muscle. The C-method may be better for preventing the bunion from returning because it better protects the muscle that stabilises the first ray.

articles.title: Revision arthrodesis after first metatarsophalangeal joint arthroplasty: A nationwide analysis of implant type and revision-related factors.
articles.authors: Arslan AK, Ulgen NK, Yigit N, Bingol I, Ata N, Birinci S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Patients who underwent first metatarsophalangeal joint arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Cumulative revision rate to arthrodesis; comparison of revision rates by implant type (total versus hemiarthroplasty); association with age and comorbidities
articles.take_home: About 1 in 5 patients who had arthroplasty of the big toe joint needed revision surgery, with most revisions happening within 2 years. Total joint replacements were more likely to need revision than partial replacements.

articles.title: Percutaneous distal metatarsal osteotomy with K-wire fixation into the medial cuneiform for hallux valgus: A case series including severe deformity.
articles.authors: Shimozono Y, Yoshida S, Mizuno Y, Funakoshi N, Matsuda S, Kobayashi M
articles.population: Patients undergoing surgery for hallux valgus (bunions), including those with severe deformity
articles.outcomes: Hallux valgus angle, intermetatarsal angle, foot function questionnaire scores, and complications
articles.take_home: A minimally invasive surgical technique using a small metal wire for fixation successfully corrected bunions, including severe cases, with good foot function outcomes and few complications. Patients could put full weight on their foot immediately after surgery.

articles.title: Establishing the UK clubfoot research priorities : a multiple-stakeholder consensus study.
articles.authors: Trees A, Baird EJ, Lockey D, Douglas C, Ashby E, Campbell DM, et al.
articles.study_type: Consensus study using modified Delphi technique
articles.population: Clubfoot stakeholders including healthcare professionals, patients and carers in the UK
articles.sample_size: 103 participants in round one, 93 in round two
articles.outcomes: Nine research priorities identified across four themes: Primary Treatment, Bracing, Relapse, and Physiotherapy. Highest priorities were comparing unilateral versus bilateral bracing and understanding relapse prevention
articles.take_home: UK experts and patients have identified the most important questions that need answering about clubfoot treatment, with particular focus on which type of bracing works best and how to stop the condition from coming back. These priorities will help guide future research trials to improve clubfoot care.

articles.title: Amputation risk after total ankle arthroplasty: A national database study with verified continued patient enrollment.
articles.authors: Louka JG, Alkaramany E, Mansur NS, Guyton GP
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary total ankle arthroplasty between 2010 and 2018
articles.outcomes: Major amputation of the lower extremity within 5 years after surgery
articles.take_home: Major amputation occurred in 0.6% of patients over 5 years after ankle replacement surgery, but diabetic patients had nearly twice the risk (1%) compared to non-diabetic patients. This suggests careful patient selection and good blood sugar control are important when considering this surgery.

articles.title: The importance of axial rotation of the lower limb : a systematic review of measurement methods.
articles.authors: Favier B, Acker A, Miles J, de Cesar Netto C, Burssens A, Goldberg A
articles.population: CT-based measurement techniques for lower limb rotation
articles.outcomes: Reliability and reproducibility of femoral version and tibial torsion measurement methods; Murphy method for femoral version and Goutallier method for tibial torsion identified as most reliable
articles.take_home: The way your thigh bone and shin bone twist affects your hip, knee and ankle health. Doctors should use standardised measurement methods (Murphy and Goutallier) when checking these twists, as these methods are most reliable and consistent.

articles.title: Coronal alignment parameters of the knee predict osteoarthritis development : a Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee classification-based analysis using the Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study data.
articles.authors: Kim JS, MacDessi SJ, Lee DW, Ro DH
articles.population: Adults without knee osteoarthritis at baseline from the Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study
articles.outcomes: Development of knee osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 or higher) over 5 years; association with coronal alignment parameters
articles.take_home: Certain measurements of how the knee is aligned in the front-to-back view were linked to a higher risk of developing osteoarthritis, particularly when the joint line angle was abnormal. The overall classification type mattered less than the specific alignment measurements themselves.

articles.title: Comparison of the modified Brostrom-Gould procedure for chronic lateral ankle instability in adolescents with and without an os subfibulare : a propensity score-matched study.
articles.authors: Xiong S, Li Y, Liu Z, Zhao F, Jiang D, Hu Y, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adolescent patients with chronic lateral ankle instability undergoing modified Brostrom-Gould procedure
articles.sample_size: 82 matched patients (41 with os subfibulare, 41 without)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported pain and function scores (VAS, Karlsson score, Tegner score, FAOS), re-sprain rates, return to sport time, satisfaction, and complications
articles.take_home: Young people with a bone fragment called os subfibulare who have ankle surgery had similar good results to those without this fragment, with both groups improving significantly. Those with high sporting demands or additional ligament damage had a higher risk of re-injury after surgery.

articles.title: Transitional talalgia after medial gastrocnemius lengthening using the Strayer technique in chronic plantar fasciitis.
articles.authors: Garcia FJV, Marrero-Hernandez A, Morales-Perez E, Somoza-Peral I, Pensado-Senoris N, Rendon-Diaz D, et al.
articles.population: Patients with chronic plantar fasciitis who underwent Strayer medial gastrocnemius recession
articles.outcomes: Postoperative heel pain patterns, VAS pain scores, patient satisfaction, complications
articles.take_home: About one third of patients experienced a new type of heel pain after surgery called transitional talalgia, but this pain was self-limiting and most patients were still satisfied with their treatment. Overall satisfaction was 84.7% and there was no evidence that this new pain pattern indicated the surgery had failed.

articles.title: Accuracy of radiology MRI reports in predicting syndesmotic injuries: An intraoperative correlation study.
articles.authors: Vacariu E, Tevere A, Shepherd D, Schneider T, Talia A
articles.study_type: Retrospective chart review with intraoperative correlation
articles.population: Patients with chronic ankle instability or pain undergoing ankle arthroscopy and MRI
articles.outcomes: MRI sensitivity 48%, specificity 100%, positive predictive value 100%, negative predictive value 25.6%, overall accuracy 56.2%
articles.take_home: MRI reports are very good at confirming syndesmosis injuries when they say one is present, but they miss about half of the injuries that are actually found during surgery. Clinicians should examine the MRI images themselves rather than relying only on the written report.

articles.title: Weightbearing after ankle fracture fixation; A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials, a modern perspective.
articles.authors: Rigney B, Storme J, Condell R, Coveney EI, Kearns SR
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.outcomes: Olerud-Molander Ankle Scores at 6 weeks and 3 months, EuroQol-5D scores at 6 weeks, complication rates
articles.take_home: Early weightbearing after ankle fracture surgery improves how well patients function and their quality of life in the first 6 weeks compared to waiting longer before putting weight on the ankle, and it does not cause more complications. These benefits disappear after 6 months, and early weightbearing works best in patients with stable fixation and good bone quality.

articles.title: Two-Stage vs Single-Stage Ilizarov Application in High-Risk Patients: Impact on Early Complications and Resource Utilization.
articles.authors: Fischer L, Viehofer A, Castroviejo C, Tsolakidis A, Zendeli F, Flury A, et al.
articles.population: High-risk patients undergoing Ilizarov external fixator treatment for foot and ankle conditions, including those with diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, obesity, renal insufficiency, infection, or Charcot arthropathy
articles.outcomes: Wound revision rates within 3 months post removal, impaired wound healing rates, hospital length of stay, total hospitalisation costs
articles.take_home: A two-stage approach to Ilizarov fixator application, where initial bony correction is done first and the ring fixator applied 5 days later, resulted in significantly fewer wound problems and revisions compared to doing everything in one operation, particularly in patients with infection or Charcot arthropathy. This benefit did not increase hospital stay or costs.

articles.title: Distal Oblique Osteotomy vs Arthrodesis for Advanced Hallux Rigidus: A Matched Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Lee JY, Koh Ern Juan J, Toh RX, Mohamed Buhary KS, Li Z, Tay KS
articles.population: Patients with advanced hallux rigidus who had failed conservative management
articles.outcomes: Patient satisfaction, complications, revision surgery rates, pain scores, AOFAS scores, and range of motion at minimum 24 months follow-up
articles.take_home: Both distal oblique osteotomy and arthrodesis provided good pain relief and patient satisfaction for advanced hallux rigidus, but distal oblique osteotomy had fewer complications and preserved joint movement. Distal oblique osteotomy may be a suitable alternative to arthrodesis for selected patients, though more research is needed.
